exercises: vendor extension keys at the document root, on info, on a path item, on an operation, on a parameter, on a schema and on a schema property
note: The prefix x-riverside- is invented for these fixtures. The point is not that the browser understands any of these keys, it is that resolution hands back the node as written. Nothing here is allow-listed, so no future extension should need the resolver to be revisited. Check this by resolving a reference and inspecting the resulting node, not only by looking at the rendered page.

expected.assert: Every x-riverside- key survives parsing and resolution byte for byte, including the nested object value on x-riverside-rate-limit and the integer on x-riverside-cache-seconds.
No unknown extension key causes an error, a warning, or a dropped node.
listBooks, its shelfMark parameter and the Book schema all render normally alongside their unknown extensions.
The browser does not need to display any of these. It must not rename, coerce or discard them.
